A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-Mini and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-H. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses in Sections 3, 5-6 and Appendices E-H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original LLaVA-Mini experiments and results, including the supplementary evaluations and case studies.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same query-based compression, modality pre-fusion, image/video processing and two-stage training. The added citation in the compression description does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora, 11 image benchmarks, seven video benchmarks, and high-resolution and long-video scenarios described in Section 5.1 and Appendix C.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments and qualitative cases. Chen et al. and mPLUG-Owl3 are newly cited but are not added as evaluated baselines; the other Ye citation changes only relabel existing references.

E3.justification: The backbones, resolutions, token configurations, training budgets and one-frame-per-second video sampling remain unchanged. Appendix C preserves the evaluation procedures and metrics, and Table 9 preserves the training settings.

E4.justification: The attention analyses, compression and pre-fusion ablations, hardware comparisons, visualizations and case studies in Sections 3 and 6 and Appendices E-G are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. For example, LLaVA-Mini's MMBench score remains 65.6 in Table 1, and its one-token A100 latency remains 38.64 milliseconds in Appendix Table 13.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), including the compression and pre-fusion definitions and Appendix A's attention calculations, are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same one-token multimodal modeling and performance/efficiency claims, including the reported 77% FLOPs reduction and capacity for over 10,000 video frames.

C2.justification: The early-layer fusion explanation, compression rationale, long-video extrapolation arguments and case-study interpretations remain unchanged. Section 3.2 adds attribution to earlier research without revising these explanations or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data processing and training information in Section 5.1 and Appendix B are unchanged. The code and model access links are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 newly acknowledges that the early-layer attention finding agrees with Chen et al. (2024). Section 4.1 adds mPLUG-Owl3, cited as Ye et al. (2024a), alongside the existing cross-attention reference. Both works are added to the bibliography; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes a small local rewrite in Section 3.2, adds reviewer and funding acknowledgments, and updates publication headers and citation suffixes. The main narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-15 and Tables 1-15 retain their displays and placement. The conference header and added acknowledgments and references produce limited text reflow and bibliography pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly attribution by explicitly connecting the attention finding to Chen et al. in Section 3.2 and adding mPLUG-Owl3 to the compression discussion in Section 4.1. These additions clarify the relationship to prior work; methods, empirical support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
